title: SaaS Security Report (formerly the Shadow IT Report, ZINS): shadow IT discovery, risk index and API surface

prose.text: Whether it also gives IoT device visibility is open {{gap:ssr-iot}}. Whether it is powered by ZIA traffic is open {{gap:ssr-zia}}. Whether it is observability only, with no enforcement, is open {{gap:ssr-enforcement}}.
{{ssr-endpoint}} {{ssr-sdk}} The GraphQL API itself, its auth and its scope are in [[shared.analytics.graphql]].

The legacy statement that neither SDK has a zins namespace is contradicted for Python {{gap:ssr-no-sdk}}. The rename history is not captured {{gap:ssr-rename}}, and the 8,500-app figure in older marketing {{gap:ssr-8500}}.

checks.do: Before comparing shadow IT counts, confirm the time period and filters; the default period is the last 7 days.
For an API question, check the zins package and the GraphQL endpoint before saying there is no SDK; the Python SDK has one.

ssr-what.statement: The SaaS Security Report breaks applications down by status, sanctioned, unsanctioned, unclassified or under review, and by their number of users.

quotes: The SaaS Security Report gives a breakdown of applications by their status — sanctioned, unsanctioned, unclassified, or under review and their number of users.

ssr-scale.statement: Zscaler says the SaaS Security Report supports up to 50K cloud applications.

quotes: Zscaler supports up to 50K cloud applications.

ssr-risk-index.statement: Each application carries a risk index from 1 (lowest risk) to 5 (highest risk).

quotes: (1–5, 1 being the lowest risk and 5 being the highest)

ssr-features.statement: Its listed benefits include discovering and managing shadow IT applications used by the organization's users, departments or locations, and scrutinizing applications across multiple risk attributes.

quotes: Discover and manage shadow IT applications used by your organization's user, department, or location.
Gain comprehensive visibility and assurance for SaaS applications by scrutinizing them across multiple risk attributes

ssr-default-period.statement: The report can show the last 1 day, 7 days, 15 days, month or quarter, and its default period is the last 7 days.

quotes: You can view data from the last 1 day, 7 days, 15 days, month, or quarter. The default time period is the last 7 days.

ssr-path.statement: The report is opened under Internet & SaaS > Analytics > SaaS Security Report > Applications.

quotes: Internet & SaaS > Analytics > SaaS Security Report > Applications

ssr-export.statement: The report can be scheduled daily, weekly or monthly, and downloaded as a CSV file.

quotes: Schedule a daily, weekly, or monthly SaaS Security Report.
Download the report as a CSV file.

ssr-endpoint.statement: The Analytics API's production GraphQL endpoint is `https://api.zsapi.net/zins/graphql`, and the API can be accessed via the OneAPI gateway.

quotes: can be accessed via the OneAPI gateway

ssr-sdk.statement: The vendored Python SDK's ShadowItAPI client targets the Z-Insights SHADOW_IT domain and posts to `/zins/graphql`.

quotes: A Client object for the Z-Insights SHADOW_IT domain.

ssr-rename.title: Whether the product was renamed from the Shadow IT Report
ssr-rename.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Renamed. Originally "Shadow IT Report" (ZINS naming), now marketed as "SaaS Security Report" in current help docs.' No captured page records the earlier name. The Python SDK calls the domain Z-Insights SHADOW_IT, which supports the ZINS alias but not the rename history.

ssr-iot.title: Whether the SaaS Security Report gives IoT device visibility
ssr-iot.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Reporting product covering Shadow IT discovery (unsanctioned cloud apps users access), IoT device visibility, and SaaS-app risk reporting.' The SaaS Security Report capture does not mention IoT devices; IoT device visibility is described by a separate capture (about-iot-report.json).

ssr-zia.title: Whether the SaaS Security Report is powered by ZIA traffic
ssr-zia.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Powered by traffic flowing through ZIA; extracts visibility signals from existing ZIA telemetry.' The capture places the report under Internet & SaaS analytics and mentions allowed and blocked transactions, but does not state its data source.

ssr-enforcement.title: Whether the SaaS Security Report enforces policy
ssr-enforcement.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Not a policy-enforcement product; pure observability.' The capture describes discovery, risk review and reporting, and says nothing about enforcement either way.

ssr-8500.title: Older catalogue size in marketing material
ssr-8500.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Some marketing material still cites the older 8,500+ figure — outdated.' No captured page gives an 8,500-application figure.

ssr-no-sdk.title: Whether the Go SDK has a Z-Insights module
ssr-no-sdk.detail: The vendored Go SDK tree has no zins package, so Go callers would use direct GraphQL with OneAPI auth; upstream Go releases newer than the vendored tree are unchecked. The Python SDK does have one (ssr-sdk).
